On top de eso, el energy shock is no longer just a short-term inflación riesgo- it has turned into a bigger debate about how sticky inflación really is y how cautiously central banks need a move de here.  El real question is no longer just whether crecimiento slows, or inflación falls, but whether politics will support or weaken el policies meant a manage both. El range de possible outcomes has widened, con tail risks playing a bigger role en shaping el regional perspectiva. Hence, nosotros are changing el order de nuestro regular monthly update a reflect where el conversations around nuestro region lie nowadays. More broadly, el region is entering a period en which political outcomes are increasingly determining macro-outcomes.

blocks.mt_text: •	Brazil's election año has not given President Lula a stable lead, even against a benign macro backdrop. A month ago, several polls showed him trailing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) en runoff simulations. El May 13 audio leak involving Flávio y recent administration policy measures have shifted el picture modestly, but a close race permanece el base case para October. El audio leak drew swift mercado y media reaction, yet polling shows el impact was contained. Flávio lost ground among moderates y swing voters en both first- y second-round simulations, but his core base held. Lula's support rose only marginally, rejection tasas stayed elevated, y centrists barely moved. Alternative opposition names — Zema (Novo), Caiado (União Brasil), Santos (MBL) — remain en low single digits, con no ready replacement a consolidate el anti-incumbent vote. Voters leaving Flávio are shifting within el opposition or opting para abstention, not migrating a Lula. El episode has also blunted Flávio's ability a anchor his campaign on corruption, a top voter concern. Where do nosotros stand on crecimiento? Crecimiento permanece uneven across el region. El common thread is a growing reliance on domestic demand y policy support rather than private inversión, leaving economies more exposed a inflación shocks, tighter financial conditions, y shifts en political sentiment.

Lula's support rose only marginally, rejection rates stayed elevated, and centrists barely moved. The common thread is a growing reliance on domestic demand and policy support rather than private investment, leaving economies more exposed to inflation shocks, tighter financial conditions, and shifts in political sentiment.

Inflación risks have become more persistent, y el bar para additional accommodation has risen significantly.

blocks.mt_text: Mercados En May, MSCI Latin America declined 4.7% m/m, while MSCI Emerging Mercados led globally con a 9.5% m/m gain. El region's underperformance was driven primarily by Brazil (-9.2% m/m), which struggled as broadening inflación pressures kept monetary policy cautious y political noise intensified around Senator Flávio Bolsonaro ahead de el 2026 race. Mexico rose 2.6% m/m con MXN appreciating 0.5%, despite Banxico's 25bp cut y rating pressure ahead de el July 1st USMCA milestone weighing on sentiment. El Southern Cone y Andean mercados outperformed, led by Argentina (+11.9% m/m) following IMF approval de its second program review y a $1bn disbursement, while Colombia, Peru, y Chile also posted gains amid key political developments. At el currency level, PEN, CLP, y MXN appreciated while ARS, COP, y BRL depreciated.

edit_log.after: Latin America enters mid-year con crecimiento holding up better than expected, but politics is now el main story shaping el macro-perspectiva. El timing matters: Colombia is heading into a tight runoff, Peru is close a its second round, Brazil is dealing con a credibility shock ahead de its own elections, y Mexico just got a ratings warning that puts more pressure on el fiscal debate. On top de eso, el energy shock is no longer just a short-term inflación riesgo- it has turned into a bigger debate about how sticky inflación really is y how cautiously central banks need a move de here. El real question is no longer just whether crecimiento slows, or inflación falls, but whether politics will support or weaken el policies meant a manage both. El range de possible outcomes has widened, con tail risks playing a bigger role en shaping el regional perspectiva. Hence, nosotros are changing el order de nuestro regular monthly update a reflect where el conversations around nuestro region lie nowadays. On politics: Political developments have become el most important source de macro uncertainty across Latin America, con election cycles increasingly shaping policy expectations y mercado outcomes. More broadly, el region is entering a period en which political outcomes are increasingly determining macro-outcomes.
